issues.location: first exponent-law proof, map that splits a function on a disjoint sum
issues.finding: The displayed image of f uses a Cartesian product of two functions, but the claimed bijection has a Cartesian product of function sets as codomain and sends f to the ordered pair of its restrictions.
issues.proposed_resolution: Write the image as the ordered pair of the b and c restrictions.

issues.location: second exponent-law proof, codomain of the currying bijection
issues.finding: The proof defines f* on the actual Cartesian product of b and c, then gives its function-set domain as the cardinal product b cardtimes c. The displayed map needs the set product; cardinalities yield the stated law.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use the set product b times c in the displayed function-set codomain.

issues.location: finite-exponent proposition for an infinite cardinal
issues.finding: The proposition includes n=0, although a to the zero is one, not the infinite cardinal a.
issues.proposed_resolution: Require 0<n in omega in the proposition; the finite-product proof then applies.

issues.location: references on source lines 60 and 70 for the strict Cantor bound
issues.finding: Both references cite the power-set/exponentiation size lemma for the strict inequality a<2^a. The referenced size lemma identifies the two cardinalities; the strict inequality follows from the Cantor corollary.
issues.proposed_resolution: Point both strict-bound citations to cantorcor while preserving their existing reference scopes.

translation_treatment: The target corrects the two displayed maps, excludes zero from the finite-exponent proposition, and cites the strict-bound corollary. The frozen source remains unchanged.
